test_title: PYST 11: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 21 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the correct option to form a meaningful sentence.

Did (a)/ offences (b)/ know (c)/ you (d)/ that men (e)/ four times (f)/ commit (g)/ driving (h)/ as many (i)/ women do? (j)/ as(k)

options.text: a, d, c, e, g, f, i, h, b, k, j
a, d, c, e, f, i, h, g, k, j, b
a, d, b, e, f, i, h, c, g, k, j
a, d, e, k, f, i, h, b, g, j, c

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To form a meaningful sentence, it is important to arrange the words and phrases in a logical and grammatically correct order.
 
• The sentence should start with the question phrase "Did you know that..." and should be coherent throughout.
 
• The appropriate order is: "**Did (a) you (d) know (c) that men (e) commit (g) four times (f) as many (i) driving (h) offences (b) as (k) women do (j)?**"
 
• Thus, **Option 1** provides the correct sequence to form a clear and meaningful sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Did you know that men commit four times as many driving offences as women do?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** This sequence misplaces "commit," which should directly follow "that men" for correct structure.
 
• **Option 3:** This sequence incorrectly places "offences" too early, disrupting the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4:** This arrangement disrupts the logical flow of the sentence, particularly by starting with the wrong phrase.
